OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept when present,
            otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is
            dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and brackets are
            stripped and 8 to 15 digits are required after the '+'. So
            '0412 345 678' is stored and returned as '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            Optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a
            syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. When
            omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'Franklin, George'
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: >-
                The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName,
                dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'G.F.'
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-

                is the upper-cased first three letters of lastName and NNNN is a
                global 4-digit zero-padded sequence equal to one more than the
                number of owners at the time of registration.
              type: string
              readOnly: true

I implemented the rule: **creating an owner is rejected with 409 when another owner has the same `lastName` and `address` (compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace), unless the request sets `sharesHousehold: true`.**

Following the project's OfficeFloor function-injection conventions (not Spring MVC controllers), the change spans:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added a `sharesHousehold` boolean (write-only, default `false`) to the `OwnerFields` schema, so the generated `OwnerFieldsDto` accepts the create-only flag.

2. **`BuildOwner.java`** — the single `@RequestBody` reader now also republishes the DTO as `Out<OwnerFieldsDto>` so a later step can read the flag (the body can only be bound once).

3. **`RejectDuplicateOwnerHousehold.java`** (new step) — reads `@Val Owner` and `@Val OwnerFieldsDto`; short-circuits when `sharesHousehold` is true, otherwise normalizes (`trim` → collapse whitespace → lower-case) `lastName` and `address` and throws a checked `DuplicateOwnerHouseholdException` if any other owner matches. Mirrors the existing `RejectDuplicateOwnerTelephone` pattern (including skip-self).

4. **`DuplicateOwnerHouseholdException` + `...Handler` + escalation YAML** — the checked exception maps to a 409 Conflict `ProblemDetail`, matching the telephone-duplicate handler.

5. **`owners.POST.yml`** — inserted the `rejectHousehold` step (under `govern: [ transaction ]`) between the telephone check and customer-code assignment.

6. **`OwnerRestControllerV1Tests.createOwnerSuccess`** — one pre-existing happy-path test posted `Franklin` at `110 W. Liberty St.`, which is exactly the seed owner's household, so the new rule correctly rejected it. I gave it a distinct address (it already used a distinct telephone to dodge the telephone rule for the same reason) and documented why.
